accuracy.evidence: Checked against DfE Development Matters (2021): 3 to 4 year olds 'write some or all of their name'; the EYFS statutory framework ELG Writing: 'write recognisable letters, most of which are correctly formed'; and the DfE Writing framework (2025) on name writing from a model and letter formation. Formation facts match Letters and Sounds / Read Write Inc. handwriting guidance: L starts at the top and goes down then along, o starts at the top and goes anticlockwise like c, e starts in the middle and goes across first. The capital-first, lower-case-rest convention is stated with its real exception (names such as Mary-Jane or McKay keep two capitals; the own-name keyboard allows a capital after a dash).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early-writing slips named in the adult text: matching a name by its first letter only (Lee, Lea, Leon, Ada, Ana, Avi each refused with the letter that differs), accepting the right letters in the wrong order (Ole refused; e L o shown as 'Says: eLo'), all-capital or all-small names and a capital in the middle (small l in the first box and big E or O later each refused with their own message), writing from the right (dropping into a later box refused), and starting letters at the wrong place (a trace that begins away from the green start dot is refused with where that letter starts).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagmyname is built on name-specific mechanics: a peg board of six look-alike name cards for Leo and then Ava, a three-box name builder that only accepts the next box on the left and checks big versus small letters, a swap puzzle that turns e L o, v a A and n e B back into Leo, Ava and Ben, a trace of Leo along sampled glyph paths that must begin at each start dot and go left to right, and a keyboard name card for the child's own name. It does not reuse 774 flagnamecap (capitals for names, days and I), 229 flagcaps, 788 flagltrfam or 345 flagabc; the 6-token shingle gate reports no flag lab above 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each rule is discovered by doing: tapping Lee gives 'Lee starts like Leo, but look at every letter', small l bounces out of the first box with 'A name starts with a big letter, a capital', the swapped tiles read out what they now say until the order matches the card, a trace started at the bottom of o is stopped with 'o starts at the top', and lifting early resets the letter. Each DONE line then states the rule (check every letter; capital first, rest small; same order every time; left to right from the start dot).

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with tempting wrong options the lab then disproves: 'Yes, it starts with L' for Lee (refused on the peg board), 'Small l' for the first letter (refused in the builder), 'Yes, the letters are all there' for e L o (the board reads eLo, not Leo) and 'At the bottom' for o (the trace only starts at the top dot). The reveal line names the right answer after each task.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Eight challenge questions, each wrong option tied to a named slip: Lee or Ada gets 'starts like Leo/Ava, but look at every letter', Ole or 'all the letters are there' gets the order message, AVA and '3, all of them' get 'only the first letter is big', ava and '0, none' get 'start with a big A/B', 'On the right' gets 'we write from left to right', 'At the bottom' gets 'o starts at the top', Eva gets 'starts with a different letter'. Checked by clicking through all options with chal.cjs.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores grade 0.1 (family limit 5.0) with very short sentences and words a 4-year-old hears daily (big letter, small letter, left to right), plus the curriculum word capital explained in place. Adult text scores grade 8.7 (limit 10.0). Lab text is one short instruction per scene and canvas labels are single words or names.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph teaches one idea (letters in one order, check every letter, capital then small letters left to right, start letters in the right place). Adult paragraphs give the EYFS and DfE references, why first-letter matching and letter order matter, the named mistakes with formation facts, and what to do at home and in the lab. The content gate finds no filler phrase.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px phone screenshots in light and dark for all five scenes: the six name cards sit in two rows of three with pegs above and 20 px names, the build boxes hold baseline-aligned letters on handwriting lines above two rows of big tiles marked big/small, the swap tiles are 86 px wide, the traced Leo fills the width with green start dots and arrows clear of each other, and the name card shows the child's name in 34 px blue. All buttons are full lbtn size and wrap.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: one button per name card ('Card that says Lee'), 'Put big L in the next box' per tile, 'Swap e and L' for each pair, 'Trace big L, starting at the top', and a full letter keyboard with BIG/small toggle, dash, Rub out and Finished. The canvas aria-label carries each scene description and every piece of feedback; challenge feedback is a role=status live region; right and wrong use ✓ and ✗ as well as colour; axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes.
